strap: A daily dispatch from the world you are entering

lead.title: The United States and Switzerland set the top rate for 25 of the 28 household roles, and the map of private pay narrows to two countries
lead.standfirst: An agency salary report drawn from more than 50,300 candidates, updated last week, shows the ceiling of the profession concentrated in a very small number of markets.
lead.body:
The household staffing agency Morgan & Mallet has updated its annual salary report, drawn from a database of more than 50,300 candidates and from placements made across the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe and the Middle East between January 2024 and October 2025. Read as a map rather than as a table, it says something blunt about where a career in private service pays. Of the 28 roles the agency tracks, the United States holds the highest recorded salary for 17 of them and Switzerland for eight. Between them, two countries set the ceiling for 89 per cent of the profession.

The American figures are led by the two posts that sit closest to the principal. A private chef and a chief of staff both reach USD 300,000. Below them come the personal assistant, the estate manager, the executive assistant and the domestic couple, each recorded at up to USD 250,000, then the butler and the house manager at USD 180,000 and the housekeeper at USD 160,000. Switzerland's strength lies elsewhere, in the roles built around children and around the fabric of the house: the maternity nurse at CHF 155,000, the governess at CHF 130,000, and the nanny, the caregiver, the family cook and the private chauffeur all at CHF 120,000, close to USD 144,000 at the 2025 average rates the agency used to convert.

The three remaining roles are instructive precisely because they are exceptions. The United Arab Emirates leads the world in one post only, the travelling nanny, at AED 600,000 or about USD 163,200. The United Kingdom holds the top rate for the laundress at GBP 90,000. Monaco leads for the personal coach at EUR 130,000. Each is a specialism rather than a general market, and each reflects a particular way of living: constant movement in the Gulf, a surviving tradition of formal linen in Britain, a dense concentration of principals in the Principality who train at home.

France sits at the other end of the same table. Across most of the 28 roles the agency records a French band of EUR 45,000 to EUR 60,000, whether the post is butler, estate manager, governess or chief of staff. The same title, with the same duties, can therefore be worth four or five times more once it crosses a border. The agency also reports that average tenure in these households has fallen from around 20 years to roughly three, and that is the mechanism by which those gaps become visible: staff move, and moving reprices them.
lead.why: Two decisions shape a private service salary more than any qualification: which role, and which country. On this evidence the second now matters at least as much as the first, and it is the one a candidate can still choose.
lead.src: Morgan & Mallet, Household Staff Annual Report 2025/26

articles.title: The Swiss school year opens this week beside Lake Geneva and will move to Gstaad in January, and the households move with it
articles.body:
The autumn term at Institut Le Rosey begins in the first days of September at the Chateau du Rosey in Rolle, on the shore of Lake Geneva, and runs to the middle of December, closing with the school's Christmas celebration, to which parents are invited. In January the entire school moves to its winter campus at Chalet Rex in Gstaad and remains there until the middle of March. In April it returns to Rolle for a spring term that ends at the close of June with graduation. The school takes pupils from the age of 8 to 18 and boards all of them. There are no day places and no weekly boarding.

Entry to the older years is decided in rounds rather than continuously. Dossiers completed by 8 October 2026 receive a decision in early November. Those completed by 26 November 2026 are answered in the middle of December. A third session takes dossiers completed by 11 February 2027 and reports in early March. For younger candidates admission is rolling, but the school advises families to register between June and September of the year before entry, because each year group and each nationality carries a quota and the quotas fill during the year. Candidates are invited to spend a day on campus and to sit entrance tests in mathematics, in English or French, and in their mother tongue.

The school does not publish its fees. It states plainly that it accepts no donations and holds no endowment, and that fees are its sole source of finance, which is how it explains its independence. It awards between three and five partial scholarships a year, selected between September and December, and no full ones. The application for financial aid alone carries a fee of CHF 500, and applicants are expected to sit in the top 5 per cent of their age group academically while also contributing to sport, the arts or humanitarian work.

For a house, the significance is the calendar rather than the fees. A school that moves campus twice a year sets the rhythm of the family that follows it: a Swiss autumn, a mountain winter, a spring back beside the lake, a travel week in October and a graduation at the end of June. Houses are opened and closed around those dates, rotas are built on them, and the October and February decision sessions fall in the same weeks in which a household is otherwise planning its winter.
articles.why: In many households the school calendar, not the office diary, is the fixed point of the year. Knowing when the terms begin and where they take place is basic planning material for whoever runs the properties.

articles.title: Starlink doubles the price of its business aviation plans, and connectivity moves out of the technology budget and into the operating budget
articles.body:
SpaceX has restructured the pricing of its Starlink Business Aviation plans, and for two of them the effect is a straight doubling. The Aviation Regional 25GB plan moves from USD 2,000 a month to USD 4,000. The Aviation Global Unlimited plan moves from USD 10,000 a month to USD 20,000. A new middle tier, Aviation Regional Unlimited, arrives at USD 12,500 a month. Existing subscribers were moved automatically on to the new plans on their first billing cycle after 7 August.

The structure of the charge matters as much as its size. The subscription bills the same amount every cycle whatever the aircraft does, so it behaves less like fuel or an hourly engine programme and more like a fixed maintenance subscription. An aircraft flown 200 hours in a year and one flown 600 hours pay identically for connectivity. For a family aircraft that sits for long stretches between school terms and summer moves, that changes the shape of the annual budget rather than simply its total.

The wider shift, as the trade press covering the change puts it, is that connectivity has stopped being an optional upgrade and become part of the ownership equation. Passengers now expect the cabin to work as an office and as a screen, and judge it against what they have at home. Installation costs are examined closely at the point of purchase. Recurring subscriptions have historically escaped that scrutiny, and at these levels they will not continue to.
articles.why: Whoever assembles the household or flight department budget will be asked why a line has doubled. Being able to explain that the plan is priced by tier and not by hours flown is the difference between reporting a problem and understanding one.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi takes its first Frieze in November and opens its Guggenheim in December, and the Gulf acquires an art calendar of its own
articles.body:
Two dates at the end of this year turn Abu Dhabi into a fixture of the international art year. Frieze Abu Dhabi holds its inaugural edition from 19 to 22 November at Manarat Al Saadiyat, with Deutsche Bank as global lead partner. Three weeks later, on 11 December, the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi opens. Designed by Frank Gehry and first announced in 2006, the building runs to more than 800,000 square feet, of which roughly 125,000 square feet is exhibition space across 30 galleries.

They arrive at the end of a season of about 16 weeks that opened in Seoul in the first days of September and closes in Miami Beach in early December. Between those points sit the Armory Show in New York from 24 to 27 September, Frieze London and Frieze Masters in The Regent's Park from 14 to 18 October, and Art Basel Paris at the Grand Palais from 21 to 25 October with 211 exhibitors from 41 countries. Until now the Gulf has been a source of buyers for that circuit rather than a stop on it.

A permanent museum of that scale, paired with a fair carrying the Frieze name, changes the direction of travel. Collections held in Gulf houses have generally been shown, valued and sold elsewhere, with the specialists, registrars and shippers flying in for the occasion. An anchor institution and an annual fair create local reasons for that expertise to settle, and local dates around which a household's own art year can be organised.
articles.why: A principal who collects will expect the household to know when the fairs open, where works travel afterwards and who handles them in transit. From this winter, two of those dates sit in the Emirates.

articles.title: Foreign nationals are now barely half the applications leaving British addresses for a second residence, and the rest are British citizens
articles.body:
Henley & Partners' Private Wealth Migration Report 2026 records a change in who is leaving the United Kingdom. So far in 2026, foreign nationals account for 53 per cent of all applications the firm processes from British addresses, leaving British citizens as almost the whole of the remainder. The firm puts the equivalent British share at 8 per cent in 2018. Applications from UK addresses rose 15 per cent between 2024 and 2025, and the United Kingdom has moved from the firm's twentieth largest source market in 2018 to consistently among its five largest.

The report attributes the shift to a sequence of policy changes rather than to any single one: the abolition of the non domiciled regime, changes to inheritance tax treatment, the closure of the Tier 1 Investor Visa, and a broader climate of fiscal uncertainty. In the framework the report introduces this year, which scores jurisdictions out of 100 across 12 weighted dimensions and 38 indicators, the United Kingdom sits at 68.3 and is classed as a competitive jurisdiction under pressure, alongside Germany at 69.7, Norway at 69.0, South Korea at 66.2 and France at 65.7.

At the top of the same table are the United Arab Emirates at 85.3, Singapore at 79.5 and New Zealand at 75.8, followed by the Cayman Islands, Cyprus, the Netherlands, Portugal, Italy and Bermuda. Italy's position rests on its flat tax regime for new residents and its inheritance tax framework, with Milan increasingly functioning as a family office centre. Greece, at 70.5, has absorbed demand displaced by Spain's closure of its golden visa and Portugal's withdrawal of the property linked route. The report's own conclusion is that when a government closes a pathway, the demand does not disappear, it relocates.
articles.why: A household that changes its principal residence changes everything downstream: contracts, payroll, visas, and which house is staffed in which season. British households are now among the most likely in Europe to be planning that move.
articles.src: Henley & Partners, Private Wealth Migration Report 2026

briefs.t: The chef at the top of the table
briefs.b: The private chef is the best paid household role recorded in the United States, at up to USD 300,000, and the United Kingdom follows at up to GBP 200,000. The United States accounts for 35 per cent of the agency's global requests for chefs, ahead of the Middle East and of France and Monaco at 20 per cent each. In Los Angeles, 41 per cent of the chefs placed hold dual certification in nutrition and culinary arts.

Global business jet departures fell 2.4 per cent year on year in the week of 17 to 23 August, while activity for the year to date remains 3.5 per cent above 2025. North America accounts for more than 71 per cent of world activity and is 4.8 per cent ahead of last year. European activity is up only 1.1 per cent for the year, and flat once Italy and Spain are removed.

The Armory Show returns to the Javits Center in New York for its 32nd edition with around 230 galleries, adding a Caribbean focus and an after hours programme. Independent 20th Century runs on the same days, for the first time in Sotheby's Madison Avenue home in the former Breuer building, with 56 exhibitors and more than 130 artists.

The British Museum shows the Bayeux Tapestry from 10 September until July 2027, the first time in nearly 1,000 years that the 70 metre embroidery has left France. Tickets through to the end of the year are already sold out. It is the kind of fixture a principal will expect to be arranged rather than explained.
